ranked_evidence.title: Levels of consciousness and healing - Release CFS
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Levels of consciousness vs Healing. This is my personal summary of the levels of consciousness described in *Power vs. Human consciousness is said to span from level 20—representing the most miserable human state—to level 1000, the realm of enlightenment, like that of a Buddha. Most people operate below the critical threshold of 200, a range marked by life-destructive patterns. This shift, according to Hawkins, happens because a single individual at a high level can energetically counterbalance many others who are below that threshold. But over the course of my journey, I’ve come to value the insights it’s offered. It can seem to suggest that one must *attain* higher consciousness rather than *unlearn* the false beliefs that obscure our natural state. We need to let go of the chase for enlightenment. To embody the level of Love (500), for example, we don’t need complex techniques. The lower levels of consciousness are rooted in resistance.

ranked_evidence.title: The Consciousness Deniers | Galen Strawson | The New York Review of Books
ranked_evidence.snippet: One of the strangest things the Deniers say is that although it seems that there is conscious experience, there isn’t really any conscious experience: the seeming is, in fact, an illusion. Some people have denied the existence of consciousness: conscious experience, the subjective character of experience, the “what-it-is-like” of experience. If someone asks what conscious experience is, you say, “You know what is from your own case.” (You can add, “Here’s an example,” and give them a sharp kick.) When it comes to conscious experience, there’s a rock-bottom sense in which we’re fully acquainted with it just in having it. What people often mean when they say that consciousness is a mystery is that it’s mysterious how consciousness can be simply a matter of physical goings-on in the brain. But to say that experience is just pizza *is* to deny that consciousness exists, for we know that conscious experience exists, we know what it is like, and we know that it isn’t just pizza.
